messages.subject_clean: affxparser now builds on OSX w/ *PowerPC*
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

just to let you know that Kasper kindly fixed the problem with
affxparser building on Mac OSX with the *PowerPC (PPC)* architecture.
This is the problem that Mark reported in his June 25 thread 'mac
compile error - affxparser'.  This means affxparser should now install
all most common platforms, i.e. Linux, WinXP, and OSX.

The fix is available not only in the devel version but also the
release version of Bioconductor.  The new release version is
affxparser v1.8.1.  See also:

  http://bioconductor.org/packages/2.0/bioc/html/affxparser.html

Note: It might take a few more days for the OSX *binary* to be
available from Bioc, but you can always build from the source.

I'm keen to hear from people using aroma.affymetrix on OSX w/ PPC.
Good news, please ;)

Cheers

Henrik

Thanks!

messages.subject_clean: [aroma.affymetrix] quick question regarding var-cov of estimates
messages.body_plain:
Hi Mark,

the quick answer is that I am indeed not sure exactly which estimate
Ben is using in affyPLM.  It is better to check with him directly and
repost here.

He covers some of the standard error estimates in his thesis:

Bolstad, B. M. Low-level Analysis of High-density Oligonucleotide
Array Data: Background, Normalization and Summarization University of
California, Berkeley,

See Section 4, and especially Eqns (4.2)-(4.4), I think.

If you look at the source code of affyPLM, and scan for
'R_wrlm_rma_default_model' and 'R_rlm_rma_default_model', which are
the two native functions aroma.affymetrix is calling.  In either case,
you see that the StdErrors are calculated as:

  rlm_compute_se_anova(Ymat, rows, cols, beta, residuals, weights,se,
(double *)NULL, &residSE, 4,
PsiFunc(asInteger(PsiCode)),asReal(PsiK));

You find the source for that function in affyPLM/src/rlm_anova.c.

By looking at the code, you should be able to figure out exactly which
estimate he uses.

Cheers

Henrik

messages.subject: Re: [aroma.affymetrix] Re: genotype call question
messages.body_plain:
Genotyping algorithms classify, typically two-dimensional, data points
into three groups AA, AB, and BB.   Some methods also call data points
NoCall, but not all.  What a particular data points is classified
depends on where the classification boundaries are.

For methods like RLMM and CRLMM that classify data in a (thetaA,
thetaB) space it is likely that data points "outside" the AA-AB-BB
region will call it AA, AB, or BB, but probably not NoCall because
that often corresponds to a too weak signal.  It is also likely that
an A is called AA, but due to noise it might be called AB, less likely
B though.  But, yes, it is reasonable to assume that the more A:s
there is relative to B:s, the more likely it is to be called AA.

/H

messages.body_plain:
Hi,

busy days... aroma.affymetrix v0.5.6 is available.  Here are the updates:

Version: 0.5.6 [2007-08-10]
o AffymetrixFileSet class defines lapply(), which causes lapply()
  to redefined as a generic function, which in turn gives some
  overhead to "standard" lapply() calls due to method dispatching.
  All standard lapply() calls are now called as base::lapply().
  Benchmarking: This changes makes fit() on SNP 10K roughly 10% faster.
o Now all generated CEL files are written with upper-case filename
  extension (*.CEL).  The main reason for this is that some other
  software don't recognize CEL files with lower-case extension (*.cel).
  Existing CEL files that are in lower case (*.cel) and that are
  generated by the package are renamed to upper case (*.CEL).
  Same thing for generated CDF files.
o BUG FIX: ArrayExplorer assumed identical sample names and color maps
  across chip types and plots.  Now the set of samples and color maps
  displayed are unique for each chip type.
o Package passes R CMD check on R v2.5.1 and R v2.6.0 devel.

For a complete history, see showHistory(aroma.affymetrix).

See group page for instructions how to update.  Any patches previously
downloaded will be deleted automatically.

/Henrik

messages.subject: aroma.affymetrix v0.6.0 released
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

aroma.affymetrix v0.6.0 is available.  You can expect better support
for Calvin (aka "AGCC") CEL files and better memory performances.
Here are the details:

Version: 0.6.0 [2007-08-17]
o Steps have been taken to support working with Calvin CEL files.  This
  is still in testing, but from first tests it looks like it is working.
o Now createFrom(..., methods="create", clear=FALSE) of AffymetrixCelFile
  will first create an empty file, and then copy all CEL data to the
  new file.  This way createFrom(..., methods="create", clear=FALSE)
  and createFrom(..., methods="copy", clear=FALSE) should give CEL
  files containing the same data.  createFrom() also accepts a vector
  of options in 'methods' (renamed from 'method') which will be tried
  in order until success.
o Now calculateResidualSet() of ProbeLevelModel only loads probe-affinity
  estimates if needed, i.e. if residuals are already calculated this
  function will return faster now.
o Now getImage() of AffymetrixCelFile defaults to no interleaving,
  i.e. argument defaults to interleaved="none".  The reason for this
  is that the previous default "auto" did not work too well and
  sometimes turned on interleaving although not needed.  So, now
  one has to use interleaved="auto" ("v" or "h") when for instance
  getting images for spatial PLM residuals where an PM-only fit was
  done to a chip with MMs (otherwise every 2nd line will be blank).
  This also affects the ArrayExplorer; you pass the 'interleaved'
  argument via the process() call.
o Added support for dChip's 'snp6.0 genome info hg18.txt' file.  Note,
  this only contains information on SNPs, not CN probes.
o MEMORY OPTIMIZATION: calculateResidualSet() of ProbeLevelModel does
  part of the work in chunks.
o MEMORY OPTIMIZATION: Made getCellIndices() of AffymetrixCdfFile more
  memory effiencent by reading and transforming data in chunks.
o MEMORY OPTIMIZATION: Made findUnitsTodo() of ChipEffectFile scan
  for units in chunks.  This would bring done memory usage to about
  5% of what is used to consume.
o MEMORY OPTIMIZATION: Now getAlleleProbePairs() of AffymetrixCdfFile
  processes the CDF in chunks in order to save memory.  Before,
  processing the GenomeWideSNP_6.CDF would consume 1.5-2.0GB RAM, but
  now it is using less than 500MB.
o MEMORY OPTIMIZATION: ArrayExplorer now garbage collects after each
  image written.  That save a few hundred MB.
o BUG FIX: Removed internal trial encoding function added by mistake
  to the previous version.
o CLEAN UP: Removed findUnitsTodo() from ExonChipEffectFile, because it
  gave the same result as the one in super class ChipEffectFile.
o Package passes R CMD check on R v2.5.1 and R v2.6.0 devel.
o Package passes all redundancy tests (see website for details on tests).

For a complete history, see showHistory(aroma.affymetrix).

See group page for instructions how to update.  Any patches previously
downloaded will be deleted automatically.

/Henrik

messages.body_plain:
Hi Jeremy,

thanks for troubleshooting and reporting this.  There are two
different problems/bugs here.

PROBLEM 1:
You're right, there is a bug/typo in process() for class
GcRmaBackgroundCorrection; the .deprecated=FALSE argument should be
added as you suggested.  The same is actually true for the
OpticalBackgroundCorrection class.

PROBLEM 2:
The error on "A %*% affinity.spline.coefs : requires numeric
matrix/vector arguments" thrown by computeAffinities() of
AffymetrixCdfFile was introduced in aroma.affymetrix v0.5.1 when I
tried to please R CMD check on R v2.6.0, because of its new (but yet
not completely correct) codeTools validation.  I leave out the details
what really happened.

I've corrected this and the bug fixes will be available in the next
release.  In the meantime, install the patches [as explain online],
i.e.

library(aroma.affymetrix)
downloadPackagePatch("aroma.affymetrix")

Then it should work again.

HOWEVER 1:
I looked at the code for computeAffinity() of AffymetrixCdfFile and
realized it is not prepared for some of the most recent probe-tab
files (because Affymetrix keep changing the filename format and
renaming and adding new data columns).  This has to be looked into and
be robustified.  FYI, I have a skeleton class AffymetrixProbeTabFile
that eventually will be used for this.  FYI 2, when Bioconductor
finalizes their annotation-data packages, it is likely that we can use
those as an alternative to probe-tab files.

HOWEVER 2:
I've tested to run GcRmaBackgroundCorrection and it now works fine for
say the HG-U133_Plus_2 chip type, but not for some other, e.g.
Mapping50K_Hind240, which gives error: "Estimating non-specific
binding parameters...; Error in vector("double", length) : vector size
cannot be NA".   You might get the same for your chip type.  I do not
know why this is; it might be because the 'gcrma' code assumes no
missing values (==sequence information).  This is also something that
has to be looked into.

Cheers

Henrik

Hi Michael.

sorry for the delay; there were several issues that needed to be
solved a long the way.

First, the reason for this is that for the packages that I have that
are *not* on CRAN/Bioconductor there are no Mac binaries available,
and your settings are to install Mac binaries.  I cannot build Mac
binaries, but someone else kindly help me to do this (for the ones
that are really necessary).

So, just retry to install again:

source("http://www.braju.com/R/hbLite.R")
hbInstall("aroma.affymetrix")

The hbInstall() function should be clever enough to detect you're
trying to install Mac binaries and then it will try to find a
workaround.  The only Mac binary provided is R.native (downloaded as
*.tgz), and you'll be the first trying to install it.  If you have a
problem with that one, we have to try something else.  All other
packages, which are pure R package (no native code), should install
automatically from *source* (download *.tar.gz files).

Let us know if it works.

Alternatively,  if you *do* have Apple Xcode Tools (version 2.4.1;
Apple's website), just do 'options(pkgType="source")' and redo the
above.  That should work.

Cheers

/Henrik
